units.leftText: Paul, a servant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of God’s chosen ones and the knowledge of the truth which is according to godliness,
units.rightText: Paul, a servant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ for the faith of God’s elect and their knowledge of the truth that leads to godliness,

units.leftText: in hope of eternal life, which God, who can’t lie, promised before time began;
units.rightText: in the hope of eternal life, which God, who cannot lie, promised before time began.

units.leftText: but in his own time revealed his word in the message with which I was entrusted according to the commandment of God our Savior,
units.rightText: In His own time He has made His word evident in the proclamation entrusted to me by the command of God our Savior.

units.leftText: to Titus, my true child according to a common faith: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ our Savior.
units.rightText: To Titus, my true child in our common faith:

units.leftText: I left you in Crete for this reason, that you would set in order the things that were lacking and appoint elders in every city, as I directed you—
units.rightText: The reason I left you in Crete was that you would set in order what was unfinished and appoint elders in every town, as I directed you.

units.leftText: if anyone is blameless, the husband of one wife, having children who believe, who are not accused of loose or unruly behavior.
units.rightText: An elder must be blameless, the husband of but one wife, having children who are believers and who are not open to accusation of indiscretion or insubordination.

units.leftText: For the overseer must be blameless, as God’s steward, not self-pleasing, not easily angered, not given to wine, not violent, not greedy for dishonest gain;
units.rightText: As God’s steward, an overseer must be above reproach — not self-willed, not quick-tempered, not given to drunkenness, not violent, not greedy for money.

units.leftText: but given to hospitality, a lover of good, sober minded, fair, holy, self-controlled,
units.rightText: Instead, he must be hospitable, a lover of good, self-controlled, upright, holy, and disciplined.

units.leftText: holding to the faithful word which is according to the teaching, that he may be able to exhort in the sound doctrine, and to convict those who contradict him.
units.rightText: He must hold firmly to the faithful word as it was taught, so that he can encourage others by sound teaching and refute those who contradict it.

units.leftText: For there are also many unruly men, vain talkers and deceivers, especially those of the circumcision,
units.rightText: For many are rebellious and full of empty talk and deception, especially those of the circumcision,

units.leftText: whose mouths must be stopped: men who overthrow whole houses, teaching things which they ought not, for dishonest gain’s sake.
units.rightText: who must be silenced. For the sake of dishonorable gain, they undermine entire households and teach things they should not.

units.leftText: One of them, a prophet of their own, said, “Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, and idle gluttons.”
units.rightText: As one of their own prophets has said, “Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, lazy gluttons.”

units.leftText: This testimony is true. For this cause, reprove them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith,
units.rightText: This testimony is true. Therefore rebuke them sternly, so that they will be sound in the faith

units.leftText: not paying attention to Jewish fables and commandments of men who turn away from the truth.
units.rightText: and will pay no attention to Jewish myths or to the commands of men who have rejected the truth.

units.leftText: To the pure, all things are pure, but to those who are defiled and unbelieving, nothing is pure; but both their mind and their conscience are defiled.
units.rightText: To the pure, all things are pure; but to the defiled and unbelieving, nothing is pure. Indeed, both their minds and their consciences are defiled.

units.leftText: They profess that they know God, but by their deeds they deny him, being abominable, disobedient, and unfit for any good work.
units.rightText: They profess to know God, but by their actions they deny Him. They are detestable, disobedient, and unfit for any good deed.

units.leftText: But say the things which fit sound doctrine,
units.rightText: But as for you, speak the things that are consistent with sound doctrine.

units.leftText: that older men should be temperate, sensible, sober minded, sound in faith, in love, and in perseverance,
units.rightText: Older men are to be temperate, dignified, self-controlled, and sound in faith, love, and perseverance.

units.leftText: and that older women likewise be reverent in behavior, not slanderers nor enslaved to much wine, teachers of that which is good,
units.rightText: Older women, likewise, are to be reverent in their behavior, not slanderers or addicted to much wine, but teachers of good.

units.leftText: that they may train the young wives to love their husbands, to love their children,
units.rightText: In this way they can train the young women to love their husbands and children,

units.leftText: to be sober minded, chaste, workers at home, kind, being in subjection to their own husbands, that God’s word may not be blasphemed.
units.rightText: to be self-controlled, pure, managers of their households, kind, and submissive to their own husbands, so that the word of God will not be discredited.

units.leftText: Likewise, exhort the younger men to be sober minded.
units.rightText: In the same way, urge the younger men to be self-controlled.

units.leftText: In all things show yourself an example of good works. In your teaching, show integrity, seriousness, incorruptibility,
units.rightText: In everything, show yourself to be an example by doing good works. In your teaching show integrity, dignity,

units.leftText: and soundness of speech that can’t be condemned, that he who opposes you may be ashamed, having no evil thing to say about us.
units.rightText: and wholesome speech that is above reproach, so that anyone who opposes us will be ashamed, having nothing bad to say about us.

units.leftText: Exhort servants to be in subjection to their own masters and to be well-pleasing in all things, not contradicting,
units.rightText: Slaves are to submit to their own masters in everything, to be well-pleasing, not argumentative,

units.leftText: not stealing, but showing all good fidelity, that they may adorn the doctrine of God, our Savior, in all things.
units.rightText: not stealing from them, but showing all good faith, so that in every respect they will adorn the teaching about God our Savior.

units.leftText: For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all men,
units.rightText: For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to everyone.

units.leftText: instructing us to the intent that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we would live soberly, righteously, and godly in this present age;
units.rightText: It instructs us to renounce ungodliness and worldly passions, and to live sensible, upright, and godly lives in the present age,

units.leftText: looking for the blessed hope and appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ,
units.rightText: as we await the blessed hope and glorious appearance of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ.

units.leftText: who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity and purify for himself a people for his own possession, zealous for good works.
units.rightText: He gave Himself for us to redeem us from all lawlessness and to purify for Himself a people for His own possession, zealous for good deeds.

units.leftText: Say these things and exhort and reprove with all authority. Let no one despise you.
units.rightText: Speak these things as you encourage and rebuke with all authority. Let no one despise you.

units.leftText: Remind them to be in subjection to rulers and to authorities, to be obedient, to be ready for every good work,
units.rightText: Remind the believers to submit to rulers and authorities, to be obedient and ready for every good work,

units.leftText: to speak evil of no one, not to be contentious, to be gentle, showing all humility toward all men.
units.rightText: to malign no one, and to be peaceable and gentle, showing full consideration to everyone.

units.leftText: For we were also once foolish, disobedient, deceived, serving various lusts and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another.
units.rightText: For at one time we too were foolish, disobedient, misled, and enslaved to all sorts of desires and pleasures — living in malice and envy, being hated and hating one another.

units.leftText: But when the kindness of God our Savior and his love toward mankind appeared,
units.rightText: But when the kindness of God our Savior and His love for mankind appeared,

units.leftText: not by works of righteousness which we did ourselves, but according to his mercy, he saved us through the washing of regeneration and renewing by the Holy Spirit,
units.rightText: He saved us, not by the righteous deeds we had done, but according to His mercy, through the washing of new birth and renewal by the Holy Spirit.

units.leftText: whom he poured out on us richly through Jesus Christ our Savior;
units.rightText: This is the Spirit He poured out on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Savior,

units.leftText: that being justified by his grace, we might be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life.
units.rightText: so that, having been justified by His grace, we would become heirs with the hope of eternal life.

units.leftText: This saying is faithful, and concerning these things I desire that you insist confidently, so that those who have believed God may be careful to maintain good works. These things are good and profitable to men;
units.rightText: This saying is trustworthy. And I want you to emphasize these things, so that those who have believed God will take care to devote themselves to good deeds. These things are excellent and profitable for the people.

units.leftText: but shun foolish questionings, genealogies, strife, and disputes about the law; for they are unprofitable and vain.
units.rightText: But avoid foolish controversies, genealogies, arguments, and quarrels about the law, because these things are pointless and worthless.

units.leftText: Avoid a factious man after a first and second warning,
units.rightText: Reject a divisive man after a first and second admonition,

units.leftText: knowing that such a one is perverted and sinful, being self-condemned.
units.rightText: knowing that such a man is corrupt and sinful; he is self-condemned.

units.leftText: When I send Artemas to you, or Tychicus, be diligent to come to me to Nicopolis, for I have determined to winter there.
units.rightText: As soon as I send Artemas or Tychicus to you, make every effort to come to me at Nicopolis, because I have decided to winter there.

units.leftText: Send Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their journey speedily, that nothing may be lacking for them.
units.rightText: Do your best to equip Zenas the lawyer and Apollos, so that they will have everything they need.

units.leftText: Let our people also learn to maintain good works to meet necessary needs, that they may not be unfruitful.
units.rightText: And our people must also learn to devote themselves to good works in order to meet the pressing needs of others, so that they will not be unfruitful.

units.leftText: All who are with me greet you. Greet those who love us in faith.
units.rightText: All who are with me send you greetings.
